notes: The BASIC text-to-video graph for the ltx-small catalog entry (WORKPLAN 18 P7c step 2). Core nodes only -- CheckpointLoaderSimple / CLIPLoader / CLIPTextEncode x2 / LTXVConditioning / EmptyLTXVLatentVideo / LTXVScheduler / KSamplerSelect / SamplerCustom / VAEDecodeTiled / CreateVideo / SaveVideo -- so it runs on the backend the panel installs with nothing added. It is the VENDOR'S OWN default workflow for this model line, node for node except the decoder (see (5) below): comfyui_workflow_templates_json/templates/ltxv_text_to_video.json as shipped inside the managed backend (ComfyUI 0.34.0), read off disk on 2026-09-16 rather than recalled. Node ids are the vendor template's own ids, deliberately, so the correspondence stays auditable. Every input name was re-confirmed against the RUNNING backend's /object_info on the same day -- none of SamplerCustom, KSamplerSelect, LTXVScheduler, LTXVConditioning or EmptyLTXVLatentVideo is in scripts/comfy-node-defs.json, and that fixture could not have answered for them (it holds 52 demand-harvested classes, not a snapshot -- see WORKPLAN 17l).
whatChangedFromTheVendorTemplate: SIX things. Three are the same contract changes every basic here makes, one is the weight choice, and two -- (5) and (6) -- are measurements. (6) makes this graph NOT the vendor's template node for node, and not the node's own defaults either: node 8's tile_size is TUNED. (1) The CHECKPOINT is ltxv-2b-0.9.6-dev-04-25.safetensors, not the vendor template's ltx-video-2b-v0.9.safetensors. Same 2B line, same all-in-one shape (944 tensors, model.* + vae.*, verified from the safetensors header before downloading), same non-distilled sampling shape -- and 6047 MiB against 8936, which on an entry whose whole purpose is a low VRAM floor is the reason. A DISTILLED build is 4255 MiB and smaller still, but distillation changes the step count and the cfg, so it is not a drop-in and it is not a basic; it is filed as WORKPLAN 18 P7c step 2a. (2) The TEXT ENCODER is t5xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors, not the vendor's t5xxl_fp16 -- 4918 MiB against 9334, and the fp8 encoder is the choice the Wan basic already ships for the same reason. (3) SaveVideo's format/codec are mp4/h264 instead of the vendor's auto/auto: the contract names mp4/h264 because that is what AE imports, and 'auto' picks WebM for an AV1 stream. (4) filename_prefix is this panel's relative prefix (an ABSOLUTE prefix is refused by folder_paths.get_save_image_path and kills the render at its last node; see the KREA2 manifest's node 474). (5) Node 8 DECODES TILED: VAEDecodeTiled, not the vendor's plain VAEDecode, MEASURED at the node's own defaults (tile_size 512 / overlap 64 / temporal_size 64 / temporal_overlap 8); tile_size has since been tuned to 256, see (6), and the other three are still the defaults. Measured 2026-09-16 on an RTX 5090, same backend, same seed, back to back: 13 882 MiB plain against 12 544 MiB tiled, 1 338 MiB saved, and 12s either way. It does NOT move the gate (12.3 GiB still needs a 16 GB card) and it was never expected to on its own; it is free headroom on a card that is also holding After Effects, which is what WORKPLAN 16b charges for. The output is not bit-identical and is not visibly different: SSIM 0.9958, PSNR 45.6 dB against the plain decode, with no error concentration at the tile seam (per-band PSNR 45.9 / 43.1 / 51.7 left to right, worst in the band holding the subject, not the band holding the seam). See WORKPLAN 18 P7c step 2d. (6) Node 8's tile_size is 256, not the node's default 512 -- the one TUNED value in this graph, and it is tuned on purpose. At 512 the job was barely tiled (16 latent columns against a 24-wide latent: two tiles), which is why (5) bought only a quarter of the decode spike. Swept 2026-09-16 on one backend, one seed, RTX 5090, every clip deterministic: 512/64 default 12 576 MiB, tile_size 256 10 272 MiB, both 12s -- 2 304 MiB saved, 3 642 against the plain decoder. temporal_size was swept too (32 -> 10 784, 16 and 8 -> 10 048, which are the SAME job because nodes.py floors the latent chunk at 2) and was REJECTED: every temporal chunk boundary shows up as a periodic per-frame PSNR dip against the plain decode (sawtooth every 8 frames at temporal_size 16, dips at frames 24/48/72 at 32) and a matching frame-to-frame luma jump -- a pulse in a user's clip, bought for under 250 MiB more. tile_size 256 alone adds no temporal dip (per-frame minimum 36.7 dB at frame 58, the same frame and value as the default), SSIM 0.9951 / PSNR 43.9 dB against the plain decode, and a x10-amplified difference image shows edge noise only, no tile grid. It still does NOT move the gate: 10 272 MiB over idle plus After Effects' own resident footprint (tiers.js AE_RESIDENT_MB, 3 255) is more than a 12 GB card holds, so whether a 12 GB card can run it is a measurement on a constrained card, WORKPLAN 18 P7c step 2f. See WORKPLAN 18 P7c step 2e. That measurement was taken the same day and it MOVED the gate 16 -> 12: the 5090 was ballasted (scripts/vram-ballast.py, real allocations) down to a 12 GB card's room with After Effects and the desktop still on it, and this exact graph ran in 12.46 s against 12.28 s unconstrained, delta 7 401 MiB against 10 394, with a byte-identical clip; with 4 966 MiB left (a 12 GB card minus AE and tiers.js DESKTOP_FREE_MB) it ran in 12.69 s, delta 3 621, identical again. The managed backend's DynamicVRAM streams weights from pinned host RAM rather than holding them resident, so the job shrinks to fit instead of grinding. See WORKPLAN 18 P7c step 2f. The vendor's two Note/MarkdownNote nodes are dropped, as every basic here drops them -- they are not executable classes. Sampler, scheduler, steps, cfg, shift, terminal, size, length and fps are the vendor's values untouched, except the seed: 12345, so a measurement is reproducible, as sd15 / sdxl / krea2 / wan22-5b all do.
whyTheNegativeIsThis: It is the vendor template's own negative, copied verbatim. Unlike Wan's, it is already English, so nothing had to be translated. The panel replaces it whenever the request carries a negative.

prompt.note: NOT reachable by the panel's usual introspection, and that is the one thing about this graph a reader must not miss. The panel follows KSampler.positive/negative back to the CLIPTextEncode pair (comfy-workflows/README.md); this graph has no KSampler -- it uses SamplerCustom, and its positive/negative come from LTXVConditioning, one hop further back. Declaring the prompt node here is what makes injection work. See whyTheNegativeIsNotDeclared.

whyTheNegativeIsNotDeclared: procedural carries only the positive because that is all the schema takes; the negative sits on node 7, one hop behind LTXVConditioning.negative the same way. If a future request needs the negative injected on this graph, that hop is the work -- it is not a missing value, it is a missing edge in the resolver's walk.
whyNoResolution: No procedural.resolution, for the reason measured on the sd15 basic and written up as WORKPLAN 18 P5a. procedural.resolution means 'this template derives its pixel dimensions from a MEGAPIXEL widget' (comfy.js injectProcedural), which is true of H3's ResolutionSelector and false of an EmptyLTXVLatentVideo that takes literal width and height -- those are injected by introspection, which is what the README contract promises.
whyNoDurationSeconds: No procedural.durationSeconds either, for the same reason the Wan basic has none: this graph carries a literal numeric `length` on node 70, which is exactly what injectParams' generic frame walk writes to (comfy.js frameKeys = length/frames/video_frames/num_frames). Declaring durationSeconds here would flip lengthIn to 'seconds' and make the panel REFUSE a frames request against a graph that takes frames.
lengthIsOnAGridOfEight: LTX-Video samples 8n+1 frames and /object_info gives node 70's `length` a step of 8 (min 1, max 16384, default 97) -- a DIFFERENT grid from Wan's 4n+1, which is why this is stated per template rather than assumed. ComfyUI does not enforce the step server-side, so a frames request that is not 8n+1 is accepted and rounded by the model rather than refused. 97 frames at the CreateVideo fps of 24 is 4.04 s, which is the clip a request naming no length gets -- already under the 6 s cap WORKPLAN 18 P3a(b) is about to impose, unlike minimax-h3's >15-minute authored default.
theTwoFrameRatesAreTheVendorsOwn: LTXVConditioning.frame_rate is 25 and CreateVideo.fps is 24, and that is not a transcription error -- the vendor's ltxv_text_to_video.json ships exactly those two numbers. The first is what the MODEL is told it is generating; the second is the container's playback rate. They are left as the vendor set them, because a basic is the shape ComfyUI ships and not a tuned one, but the authored clip length follows the CONTAINER rate (97/24 = 4.04 s), which is what AE will import.
licenseIsNotApacheAndTheOwnerShouldKnow: The checkpoint's own safetensors metadata carries the 'LTXV Open Weights License 0.X' (license date April 15, 2025, covering every LTXV release since v0.9.6), NOT Apache-2.0 as Wan 2.2 is. The panel never redistributes a weight -- a user downloads it from Lightricks' own HuggingFace repo -- so this is a question about what the panel RECOMMENDS, not about what it ships. Flagged for the owner in WORKPLAN 18 P7c step 2b; no pass should decide it.

panelIntegration.promptInjection: declared: procedural.prompt -> node 6. Introspection cannot find it -- there is no KSampler in this graph (see procedural.prompt.note).
